tools.name: Claude Code
tools.purpose: Anthropic's coding agent (desktop app and CLI): implementation, review, the Superpowers process and the sa-* multi-agent workflows.

tools.name: Git
tools.purpose: Local source version control.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.purpose: JavaScript runtime for local applications and companion processes.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.purpose: Source code, pull requests and workflow coordination. The TOKYO-BEANS organization is on GitHub Team. The organisation ruleset `TOKYO-BEANS baseline` requires a pull request and blocks force-pushes and deletion on every repository, future ones included; each repository's `Stack Atlas checks` ruleset, written by the Stack Atlas standard, requires its Depot CI checks, the Semgrep check and the CodeQL code-scanning rule (errors, and security alerts high or higher, block the merge). The organisation security configuration `TOKYO-BEANS standard` (all repositories, default for new ones) turns on Secret Protection (push protection and validity checks) and Code Security (CodeQL default setup on GitHub-hosted runners: a permanent exception to Depot-only CI), and keeps Dependabot alerts and security updates off. Dependabot does version updates only, from the standard's `.github/dependabot.yml`. The owner buys Secret Protection and Code Security when the Advanced Security trial ends, about 28 November 2026.

tools.name: Graphify
tools.purpose: Indexed code definitions, callers, dependencies and change impact.

tools.name: Superpowers
tools.purpose: Development process skills: clarify intent, plan substantial changes, find root causes, change behaviour test-first, review and verify results.

tools.name: TypeSafe / Jev
tools.purpose: Typed semantic decisions: Choice for routing and candidate selection, Noul for independent yes/no judgments, Score for graded fit. Batch independent questions, retain evidence and model identity, and evaluate abstentions before automation.

feed.updater: Pinned models move through the version watch.

tools.name: Jev Router
tools.purpose: Jev picks the cheapest model that can do each new prompt (Haiku, Sonnet or Opus 5.5) with one TypeSafe call per prompt; the tool loop keeps it. In the Claude desktop app and terminal REPLs it runs as the local jev-turn-router plugin (a Claude Code mod: turn.start asks Jev, turn.step names the model), so sessions keep opus[1m]'s 1M window and tool search; plain -p and SDK jobs, subagents and hand-picked models are left alone. jev-claude (gargpratyush/jev-router, a pinned checkout with local fixes behind a key-safe launcher) does the same for a terminal through a loopback proxy. Prompt text goes to TypeSafe.

tools.name: REA
tools.purpose: Reverse Engineer Anything: a local MCP server and CLI (npm rea-agents) for understanding shipped software without its source. It inspects .NET assemblies, PE/ELF metadata, JavaScript/Electron apps, archives and installers, SQLite snapshots and saved HAR/SAZ captures, and decompiles native binaries through Ghidra, IDA or Hopper. Results carry Evidence IDs and explicit unknowns.

tools.name: Cookbook
tools.purpose: Task-to-tool recipes and the list of tools in the stack (catalog.json), which Stack Atlas follows.

tools.name: doctor-plus
tools.purpose: A skill that runs Claude Code's /doctor, then audits the workspace's instructions against the context-engineering shifts that came with the Claude 5 models. It reports first and fixes only on approval.

tools.name: skill-creator-plus
tools.purpose: A skill that audits, creates and improves Agent Skills against Anthropic's authoring practices, with a standard-library Python validator and scaffolder. Audit mode reports each rule as pass or fail with file and line evidence and changes nothing until approved.

tools.name: savvy-flow
tools.purpose: A user-invoked skill (/savvy-flow:savvy-flow): the session model plans, owns the design and reviews while five tiered worker subagents implement. An owner-requested alternative for exploratory builds; sa-build stays the default for a written plan.

tools.name: claude-reflect
tools.purpose: Turns corrections typed at the prompt into saved rules: a model check on each short prompt finds reusable corrections, and a row above the prompt saves one to the project's CLAUDE.md on a press. Used as its reflect-mod mod only; its Python hooks plugin is not installed here.

tools.name: Release Maintenance
tools.purpose: After every merge or deploy: verify the exact commit's trusted CI checks, the deployed version and health before calling the release done, and record the evidence with the release verifier.

tools.name: Stack Atlas CLI
tools.purpose: Claude's command-line route into the Stack Atlas dashboard: `atlas status` (the needs-you items, sync state and the fixer's last result as compact JSON), `atlas sync` (the dashboard's Sync) and `atlas record get|set` (only `Claude Code: <tool>` records, with a revision check and dated evidence). It runs through `with-key.mjs` with its own Cloudflare Access service token, revocable apart from the companions' token. It never approves cards, deploys, changes tools, plans or billing, or touches Access. The signed-in browser is the fallback.

tools.name: Release Verifier
tools.purpose: Hosted release verifier that validates release evidence and keeps the release ledger.

tools.name: Cloudflare
tools.purpose: Host applications, storage and access services.

tools.name: Wrangler
tools.purpose: Manage and validate Cloudflare application configuration.

tools.name: Depot
tools.purpose: Standard CI: Depot CI runs workflows in .depot/workflows, with remote container builds, caching, test reporting and failure diagnosis. GitHub stays the source and pull-request platform.

feed.updater: Installed from the depot/cli Windows release archive: unpack the new release into %LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/Depot.

tools.name: Claude Design
tools.purpose: Anthropic's design canvas and the default for sketching and designing anything visual: two or three options on a canvas, then the chosen one is built in the repository.

tools.name: Wix
tools.purpose: Website builder and host with business apps (bookings, store, pricing plans, forms, blog, members). The official Wix plugin gives Claude the Wix MCP server and skills (wix-manage recipes, wix-docs, wix-headless-kit and others) to read and change a Wix site's business data and to build code sites on Wix hosting. In the stack as an owner-approved exception for sites that already live on Wix; Cloudflare stays the default host for anything new.

feed.updater: The Claude app installs and updates the Wix plugin; its plugin.json shows the installed version.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.purpose: Adobe's generative-AI web app (firefly.adobe.com, the owner's Adobe account), used to sharpen soft real photos through the quick action "Upscale and improve image" at 4K (30 generative credits a photo, partner models). In the stack as an owner-approved exception, chosen on 10 November 2026 after it beat Nero AI Unblur on two test photos; it replaces no tool in the stack. The plan started as a 7-day free trial, so keeping the paid plan is the owner's decision.
tools.recipe: Photos (Adobe Firefly and Adobe for creativity)

tools.name: Adobe for creativity
tools.purpose: Adobe's official hosted connector (MCP server https://adobe-creativity.adobe.io/mcp, OAuth with an Adobe account) and Claude plugin that bring Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Firefly, Express, Acrobat, InDesign, Premiere and Stock actions into Claude: image adjustments, auto tone, presets, background removal, PDF, font and video tools. Connected by the owner on 10 November 2026 and loaded in a Claude Code session with 116 tool names, none that upscales or sharpens; connected but not yet used for a task, so a trial. Photo sharpening stays on the Adobe Firefly route.
tools.recipe: Photos (Adobe Firefly and Adobe for creativity)

tools.name: be-ambitious
tools.purpose: A skill that raises a task or prompt along altitude (the goal beyond the goal), depth (expert-level work checked by an outside judge) and range (methods from other fields), writes the plan and a rewritten prompt, then does the work when handed a task.

tools.name: gauntlet-loop
tools.purpose: A skill that turns a goal into one paste-ready loop prompt: set a concrete quality bar, split the work, run a builder and a separate critic on each piece, compare blind against the bar and loop until it wins. It writes the prompt; it does not run it.

tools.name: savvy-progress
tools.purpose: A mod with a progress bar above the prompt for savvy-flow and an agents panel (/agents-info) of running, finished and planned subagents with model, progress, context, estimated cost and time.

tools.name: cache-tax
tools.purpose: A mod that keeps the 1-hour prompt cache warm with model pings during breaks (/keepwarm) and shows the estimated cost before a send to a cold cache. Warming spends tokens. Installed from a reviewed, pinned copy in the local claude-local marketplace, guard set to warn.

tools.name: prompt-band
tools.purpose: The band above the prompt: a local mod that merges ribbon (robonuggets/ribbon: 7-day and 5-hour usage left, cache warm or cold, next-message cost) and session-band (JohnnyVizz/claude-kit: turn, speed, turn and session cost, context fill) into a limits row and a session row, and passes the band on so the claude-reflect, savvy-progress and cache-tax rows still show.

tools.name: context-mode
tools.purpose: Keeps large tool output out of the context window in every session: a user-scope plugin whose hooks index big Bash, Read, MCP and web results into a local SQLite FTS5 store (~/.context-mode) and return the best-matching parts, with ctx_execute, ctx_batch and ctx_search to run code and look things up without dumping raw output. Local only; no telemetry.

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.purpose: Hosted page extraction, crawling, document parsing, paper and code indexes, and Alexandria data.

feed.updater: From an elevated PowerShell outside Claude's container: npm install -g firecrawl-cli@latest

tools.name: Parallel
tools.purpose: Focused public research, synthesis and enrichment.

feed.updater: From an elevated PowerShell outside Claude's container: npm install -g parallel-web-cli@latest

tools.name: OpenSEO
tools.purpose: SEO research for websites: site audits, keyword research and clustering, competitor and backlink research, local SEO and reports, through the official OpenSEO plugin.

tools.name: AgentShield
tools.purpose: Read-only, advisory scan of agent configuration (permissions, hooks, MCP configuration, skills, secrets) on a sanitized copy; reports only findings new since the baseline and never changes anything.

tools.name: Aikido
tools.purpose: Safe Chain only: the malware and minimum-age check that runs before every npm and pip install in CI, Windows jobs included. It needs no account. The Aikido GitHub apps, Claude Code plugin, dashboard feed and CI API are not part of the stack.

feed.updater: Safe Chain moves through a standard bump.

tools.name: Semgrep
tools.purpose: Semgrep Free Edition as the dependency gate on every commit: the Depot `semgrep` job runs `semgrep ci --supply-chain` and fails only on a reachable vulnerable dependency of high or critical severity. CodeQL scans the code; Semgrep's code rules are not part of the gate. Free limits: 10 private repositories, 10 contributors.

feed.updater: The standard pin moves through a standard bump.

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.purpose: Local secret detection when vetting outside code before installing it (a download, an add-on, a copied folder), with a config you control. Never part of CI: GitHub Secret Protection blocks leaked keys at push.
tools.recipe: Connecting a new app or service

tools.name: Trivy
tools.purpose: Local infrastructure-config (misconfiguration) scan at high and critical severity when vetting outside code before installing it. Never part of CI.
tools.recipe: Connecting a new app or service

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.purpose: Local dependency vulnerability scan of lockfiles when vetting outside code before installing it, with `--no-ignore` and a config you control. Never part of CI: Semgrep Supply Chain gates the repositories' own dependencies.
tools.recipe: Connecting a new app or service

tools.name: sa-build
tools.purpose: Build a written plan task by task: one implementer and one reviewer per task, then a green PR

tools.name: sa-debug
tools.purpose: Debug a reproducible bug: evidence, Graphify trace, one hypothesis, failing test first, fix, then sa-review

tools.name: sa-deploy
tools.purpose: Prepare a Worker deploy at a merged SHA and stop for the owner; deploy only with that approval

tools.name: sa-onboard
tools.purpose: Run the stack-atlas-onboard skill on one repository: a dry run first, then the real run on request

tools.name: sa-release
tools.purpose: Release check of a merged commit or a deployment, or an owner-approved merge-when-green

tools.name: sa-research
tools.purpose: A cited answer to a public question: Parallel Search first, Firecrawl for gaps and technical answers

tools.name: sa-review
tools.purpose: Evidence-first review of a commit range: tests, Semgrep, CI and Graphify first, then one reviewer

tools.name: sa-triage
tools.purpose: Triage current Semgrep findings: parsed in code, one triager per rule group, one fix PR for the owner
